content: Rice Blast symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions on leaves with gray centers and brown borders. Lesions may coalesce causing large blighted areas. On stems, lesions are elliptical and can cause neck blast panicle blighting.

Rice Blast treatment: Apply Tricyclazole (75% WP) at 0.6g/L or Isoprothiolane (40% EC) at 1.5ml/L as foliar spray. For organic farms, use Trichoderma viride (2g/L) or Pseudomonas fluorescens (5g/L). Remove and destroy infected plant debris.

Rice Blast prevention: Use resistant varieties (e.g., improved basmati types). Maintain balanced nitrogen fertilization. Avoid dense planting. Ensure proper water management - avoid prolonged standing water. Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride before planting.
Rice Brown Spot symptoms: Small, oval to circular brown spots on leaves, sometimes with yellow halo. Spots may have gray or white centers. Severe infection causes leaf yellowing and drying.

Brown Spot treatment: Apply Mancozeb (75% WP) at 2.5g/L or Carbendazim (50% WP) at 1g/L. Improve soil fertility as brown spot is often associated with nutrient-deficient soils. Ensure balanced NPK fertilization.

Rice Bacterial Blight symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaf tips and edges that extend inward. Yellow to white stripes along leaf veins. Bacterial ooze (yellow droplets) on leaf surface in humid conditions.

Bacterial Blight treatment: No direct chemical cure. Use copper-based bactericides (Copper hydroxide 77% WP at 2g/L) for suppression. Remove infected plants. Use resistant varieties. Maintain proper water management.
